log-rank χ² = 1,596 (1 df) · p = 0.00 · stratified by study, 2 strata · pooled p = 0.00
47 patients are in more than one curve; the test assumes the groups share no one, so its p is approximate
Left out of the survival analysis (OS_MONTHS / OS_STATUS), as on cBioPortal — a patient enters only with both a status and a time of at least 0, so a missing
status is never read as censored: “TP53 mut”: 57 patients with a status but no usable time; “TP53 wt”: 57 patients with a status but no usable time. OS from
each study's own baseline (left truncation applies; baselines are NOT harmonized across studies) Status '0:...' treated as censored. 47 patients are in more
than one cohort, so in more than one curve; the log-rank test assumes the groups share no one, so its p is approximate. The log-rank test is STRATIFIED by
study (2 strata contributed events): each study is compared only against itself, so a difference in case mix between studies cannot masquerade as a
difference between cohorts. The pooled p is shown alongside — where the two disagree, the stratified one is the honest answer. Every site contributes only
(months, event, n) counts; no patient-level survival time crosses an instance boundary.
